meta.title: R3 shadow stack — the binding contract
meta.status: CONTRACT ONLY — NO ASSET PRODUCED, NO IMAGE REQUEST AUTHORISED
meta.purpose: R3 reproduces every geometry-bound raster layer for the approved target figure. It is a separate shadow stack, default OFF, that never modifies R2.
meta.note: Nothing in this file authorises a generative call. Each future call needs its own owner authorisation and its own one-shot claim.

targetFigure.role: THE CLOTHED TARGET FIGURE — the desired default appearance, identity and visible geometry

authoringBase.role: THE INTERNAL GARMENT-AUTHORING / FITTING BASE — tight neutral top, shorts, bare legs and feet
authoringBase.storagePolicy: BINDING, per D-127 §2: H1 must NEVER be tracked in git, never published, and never placed under assets/ or any other deployable path. This contract stores its filename, role, sha256, byte count, dimensions and measured anchors — never the image.
authoringBase.storageIntended: D-127 §2's intended home is the external artefact archive outside both clones, alongside the D-121 artefacts.
authoringBase.storageObserved: VERIFIED READ-ONLY on 2026-09-09, correcting the earlier observation recorded under D-132: the canonical, owner-approved H1 IS in the external archive D-127 §2 intends, at DenSejeApp-artefacts\d-131-fitting-base-v1-adoption\fitting-base.H1.png — exactly the path fitting-base-spec-v1.json -> storage.externalPath has always named — and refined.raw.png is likewise in d-121-refinement-result\. The copy under tools/avatar/build/fitting-base-head-only-review/ is a gitignored WORKING/REVIEW copy, not the canonical store. D-127 §2 was satisfied all along and its binding policy was never breached.
authoringBase.storageCorrectedBy: D-133 §1. The earlier text stated as a verified observation that H1 was not yet in the external archive; that was wrong. The D-132 register row is left verbatim — the register is append-only — and this field carries the correction.
authoringBase.storageNoMoveAuthorised: This contract moves, copies and deletes nothing. Relocating the known copy into the external archive is its own owner decision.
authoringBase.notAnatomicalGroundTruth: H1 does not reconstruct the body hidden under the target figure's clothing. It is an authoring model, never ground truth.

rawProvenance.role: RAW PROVENANCE of the target figure — the unretouched D-121 output
rawProvenance.relationToTarget: Geometrically identical to the target: 0 differing silhouette pixels, 0 differing pixels inside the solid figure, identical global anchors. The two differ ONLY in transparent and semi-transparent edge pixels (soft-alpha pixel count 27195 -> 6910).
rawProvenance.softAlphaDefinition: soft-alpha pixel = 0 < alpha < 128, i.e. a pixel that is neither fully transparent nor solid under the D-071 convention (solid = alpha >= 128). Both counts above are measured with exactly this definition over the full 1024x1536 canvas.
rawProvenance.softAlphaStatus: PROVENANCE / CLEANUP EVIDENCE ONLY. The 27195 -> 6910 figure documents the alpha cleanup between refined.raw.png and the tracked target. It is NOT a new universal R3 acceptance threshold, it gates nothing, and no R3 asset is required to reach any particular soft-alpha count.

pairEvidence.statement: All stable and reproducibly measurable global, head and arm anchors agree. No material geometric drift has been demonstrated.
pairEvidence.notClaimed: This is NOT a claim that the whole body's anatomy is identical, nor that all body proportions are preserved within 1-2 px. That cannot be proven under different clothing.

crotchProxy.what: The measured crotch proxy differs by about 12 px between the target figure and H1.
crotchProxy.nature: Clothing-sensitive and anatomically ambiguous: the target wears trousers and H1 wears shorts, so the proxy does not locate the same landmark on both images.
crotchProxy.triggers: nothing — it must not trigger generation, warp, repair or promotion
crotchProxy.noTolerance: No tolerance is defined for it. It is reported, never gated.

architecture.name: R3 shadow
architecture.optIn: explicit local opt-in only, never a cohort or percentage
architecture.r2Guarantee: R2 stays active and byte-identical. No existing R2 file is overwritten or modified.
architecture.rollback: a single controlled switch; no data migration; no Supabase or student-data change

identityCoverage.note: Coverage is NOT widened in this migration. The other five body_type x skin_tone combinations keep the existing fallback. Widening needs its own decision.

layerContract.background: fully transparent; no background, no shadow, no glow

paintOrder.rule: The BINDING part of this layer contract is the RELATIVE paint order below, bottom to top. Numeric z-index values are NOT part of it — see zIndices, which are provisional and unapproved.
invariants: the technical underlay is the bottom layer of the figure
the three default clothing layers paint above the underlay
a cosmetic torso garment paints above the default tee, because the tee is now its own layer instead of being baked into the base
hair paints above every face layer and every clothing layer

zIndices.status: APPROVED by D-135 — see zModel for the full binding map, its ties and its semantics
zIndices.supersededProvisional: D-132 recorded tee 6, trousers 7, shoes 8 and torso 20 as PROVISIONAL examples. D-135 replaces 6, 7 and 8 with 10, 11 and 12 because 6 and 8 are already taken INSIDE R3's own map by the eyes cosmetic and the face cosmetic; torso stays at 20. D-132's note that 6 and 8 collide with the live R2_COSMETIC_Z is corrected in zModel.crossStackOverlap — a cross-stack overlap is harmless, because the three stacks never share a DOM.

slots.content: technical underlay: tight neutral top, shorts, bare legs and feet, BALD, BLANK FACE

slots.note: iris multiply x token, fixed on top
cosmetic garment; must occlude the tee layer

layerContract.newSlotsRationale: R2 bakes the t-shirt, trousers and sneakers into its base layer. R3 makes them separate layers, so the default outfit becomes removable and the occlusion contract changes from 'garment occludes a baked tee' to 'garment occludes a separate tee layer'.

zModel.status: CONTRACT ONLY — NO RUNTIME CONSTANT, RESOLVER, COMPOSITOR OR MANIFEST WIRING IS CREATED

independence.rule: R3 gets its OWN R3_STACK_Z, R3_COSMETIC_Z and any separate overrides. They must not import, alias or dynamically derive values from R2_STACK_Z, R2_COSMETIC_Z or C2_LAYER_Z.
independence.sameNumberIsNotInheritance: Where an R3 number equals an existing R2 number it is INDEPENDENTLY PINNED to the same numeric value — it is not inherited. A later change to an R2 constant must never move an R3 layer.
independence.notCreatedHere: D-135 does not create the constants. It fixes what their values must be when they are created.

slots.note: one logical slot holding two sublayers — see approvedTies
the blink engine's lids, stamped by the engine itself
glasses; below the hair so the fringe covers the upper rim
masks; per-item overrides may raise it
garment / equipment; above all three default clothing layers

uniqueness.rule: INDEPENDENTLY SORTED LOGICAL SLOTS must not have unintended z collisions. Approved internal SUBLAYERS of one logical slot MAY share a z, provided their DOM order is explicit and binding.
uniqueness.notBlanketUniqueness: This is deliberately NOT a claim that every raster layer has a unique z. A blanket-uniqueness test would be wrong and must not be written: it would fail the approved eyes tie below.
uniqueness.perItemOverridesAreNotTies: A per-item override (panda-mask at 41) is an alternative z for the SAME logical slot, chosen per item. It is not a tie and never coexists with that slot's default value.

approvedTies.domOrder: iris is inserted FIRST, eyes-fixed SECOND
approvedTies.why: Equal z means DOM order decides, and the fixed highlight must paint on top of the tinted iris. The existing R2 stack emits them in exactly this order, deliberately.

faceSlotSemantics.verified: Verified read-only against js/avatar-expression-engine.js and avatar.html on 2026-09-10.
faceSlotSemantics.finding: On the decomposed raster path the expression engine does NOT create an overlay: _initOverlay() takes this._overlay = container.querySelector('[data-c2-layer="face"]') with _ownsOverlay = false, and swaps that layer's src in place. The separate .avatar-expr-overlay element, which avatar.html stamps to zIndex 3, exists only on the C2/SVG path, where there is no decomposed face raster.
faceSlotSemantics.conclusion: exprOverlay is the OPERATIVE REPRESENTATION OF THE SAME LOGICAL FACE SLOT, not a second element at z=3. On the R3 path the expression engine must borrow the decomposed face layer in place, exactly as it does today on R2, so no two elements ever occupy z=3 in one mounted stack and there is no DOM-order tie to pin here.
faceSlotSemantics.requirement: If a future change ever makes them coexist, their internal DOM order must be fixed explicitly by a new decision before that ships.

paintOrder.bindingBoundaryOrder: base < tee < trousers < shoes < torso < hair < headwear
consequences: trousers paint over the tee wherever they overlap around the waist
shoes paint over the trousers wherever they overlap around the ankles
a torso garment or equipment asset may paint over all three default clothing layers where the asset extends into their areas
hair paints above every face and clothing layer; headwear above the hair
paintOrder.intentional: This order is deliberate, not incidental. The overlaps it resolves are the waist, the ankles and a garment that extends past the tee.

d134StillApplies.rule: The z order NEVER overrides D-134. Every torso or equipment asset remains subject to R3_ARM_HAND_PROTECT(asset).
d134StillApplies.explicit: Painting above the clothing layers does not grant permission to paint over exposed arms or hands. Z order may not be used to bypass the arm/hand protection or an asset-specific intentional-coverage decision, which remains the only way that protection narrows.

stackSelection.isSemanticsNotSyntax: That expression states the required semantics. The concrete later syntax may differ.
stackSelection.resolverContract: An R3 resolver may return EITHER a complete, validated R3 layer list OR null. It must never return an empty or partial list as success.
stackSelection.noMixing: No geometry-bound R2 and R3 layers may be mixed to fill in missing R3 assets. If the required R3 composition is not complete, the WHOLE avatar stack falls back to R2, and then to C2.
stackSelection.atomicity: The choice is atomic and per render: one stack is mounted, never a blend of two.
stackSelection.doesNotWidenReuse: D-135 does not widen which existing cosmetics or assets are approved for reuse. It fixes stack selection and z semantics only.

crossStackOverlap.rule: The same numeric z may appear in the R3, R2 and C2 maps. That is NOT an error and must not be tested as one.
crossStackOverlap.why: The three stacks are never mounted as independent avatar stacks at the same time — the renderer mounts exactly one layer list — so their numbers can never meet in one DOM.
crossStackOverlap.correctionOfAnEarlierNote: D-132's zIndices note said the provisional 6 and 8 'collide numerically with the live R2_COSMETIC_Z'. That framing was wrong: an R2/R3 cross-stack overlap is harmless. The real defect was INSIDE R3's own map, where 6 and 8 are taken by the eyes cosmetic and the face cosmetic — which is why D-135 moves the clothing to 10, 11 and 12.

externalSurfaces.requirement: The external expression and blink surfaces must later be driven by the stack that was ACTUALLY mounted, so a stack switch never leaves a stale overlay behind — the same discipline the blink profile already follows on the R2/C2 split, extended to three ways.
externalSurfaces.notImplementedHere: D-135 states the requirement. It does not implement it.

zModel.authorisation: D-135 authorises no image request and creates or consumes no claim. It creates no runtime constant, resolver, compositor or manifest wiring, no mask, no region and no asset.

irisContract.status: CONTRACT ONLY — NO IRIS MAP PRODUCED, NO RUNTIME CONSTANT CREATED, NO IMAGE REQUEST AUTHORISED

method.binding: The R3 iris is ONE independently generated ACHROMATIC greyscale/luminance map, multiplied by ONE independently pinned R3 colour token, with the fixed-eyes layer on top in D-135's binding eyes order.
method.isOneAssetPlusOneToken: One visual asset plus one deterministic design token — not two assets, and not a token on its own.
method.notFullColour: It is NOT a full-colour iris asset.
method.notProcedural: It is NOT a procedurally drawn iris.
method.layerOrder: The iris sublayer is composited first and the fixed-eyes sublayer second, both on the eyes slot at z=4, exactly as zModel.approvedTies pins it.

token.name: R3_IRIS_DEFAULT
token.independentlyPinned: R3 pins this value for itself. It must never be imported from, aliased to, or dynamically derived from R2_IRIS_DEFAULT — the same discipline zModel.independence applies to the z maps.
token.whySameValue: The same number is chosen because it is already the documented Master-brown DESIGN value in the established R2 precedent. Reusing a documented design value is not using an old R2 asset as a pixel source.
token.notMeasuredFromFinishedPixels: The token is NOT claimed to be derivable from the finished iris pixels of any figure. The displayed colour is a product of BOTH the token AND the map's luminance, so no single rendered pixel yields the token. Any future re-measurement would be its own decision and would have to state its method.
token.notCreatedHere: D-136 does not create the runtime constant. It fixes what its value must be when it is created.

renderPair.rule: The token alone guarantees nothing about visual colour fidelity. The future luminance map and the token work as ONE render pair, and only their composed result can be judged.
laterApproval: the finished, composed and tinted iris result is what is assessed
after the automatic format and layer checks
renderPair.noAfterTheFactTolerance: No tolerance may be invented after the result is seen, and there is no automatic recolour, warp or repair.
renderPair.doesNotAuthoriseTheCall: D-136 does not authorise the later image call and pre-registers no candidate-specific pixel thresholds yet.

tintSupport.noUntintedFallback: R2's untinted fail-soft rendering is NOT carried over to R3. An untinted greyscale iris map is not the approved R3 appearance and must never be shown.
tintSupport.incompleteMeansNull: If the required mask/multiply mechanism is unsupported, or the tinted iris layer cannot be established correctly, the R3 stack is NOT complete and the future R3 resolver must return null.
tintSupport.fallbackChain: D-135's atomic fallback then applies: R3 -> R2 -> C2.
tintSupport.noMixing: No R3 and R2 eyes layers may be mixed, and no untinted R3 iris map may be displayed.
tintSupport.contractNotImplementation: This is contract now, not runtime implementation.

noEyeColourSystem.rule: D-136 introduces no user-selectable eye colour, no new identity field, no persistence or Supabase field, no additional iris colours and no eye-colour UI.
noEyeColourSystem.scopeOfTheToken: R3_IRIS_DEFAULT is only the fixed neutral default value.
noEyeColourSystem.separateDecision: A real EYE_COLOR feature needs its own later owner decision.

budget.effect: Locking asset 7 to one generative call moves the derived image-call budget from 14-16 to 15-16.
budget.stillNotAuthorisation: The budget remains planning, never consent. Every call needs its own owner authorisation and its own one-shot claim.

firstSliceMembership.why: The first slice is an isolated structural proof of geometry, alpha, layering, eyes, hair and the default clothing. Blush adds a different failure class — a blend mode — and its production path is not yet settled, so including it would couple two open questions inside one proof and make a failure impossible to attribute.

it may not be selected by the runtime resolver
it may not be used for canary, deploy or promotion

blushStaysMandatory.notWeakened: Excluding blush from the first slice says nothing about the finished stack. A complete R3 stack without blush is not complete.

occlusionContract.armHandInvariant: An R3 torso or equipment layer must NEVER unintentionally paint over exposed arms or hands. Whatever the final paint order and z values turn out to be, the visible arm and hand pixels of the approved underlay stay visible unless an approved garment is deliberately authored to cover them.
occlusionContract.whyItChanged: In R2 the torso garment sits immediately above the base and its artwork is authored against that exact baked silhouette. In R3 the torso garment sits above a separate tee layer, so it passes over more of the body and arm/hand exposure is no longer protected by its low position alone.
occlusionContract.prerequisite: The R3 occlusion/protect contract — which regions a torso or equipment layer MAY cover, and which arm and hand regions it MAY NOT — must be PRE-REGISTERED and owner-approved BEFORE armor-knight or any other torso equipment is produced or integrated. It is a precondition of that work, never a check applied afterwards.
occlusionContract.fittingBaseMaskIsNotRuntime: The existing fitting-base arm/hand protect mask is a fitting-base FIXTURE. It is NOT automatically an R3 runtime mask and carries no runtime authority. Any use of it as a reference or control when producing R3 assets must be documented and approved separately.
occlusionContract.authorisation: This clause is contract text only. It authorises no mask to be created, changed, derived or promoted, and no image call.

differenceAnalysisMayBe: detecting leakage outside an intended region
validating a finished R3 composition against the target
differenceAnalysisMayNotBe: a pixel source for the tee, trousers or shoes
evidence that the layers are cleanly separable
pixelSourcePolicy.why: A difference shows that pixels differ, not which garment they belong to. Measured read-only, the difference between the target and H1 forms ONE DOMINANT CONNECTED REGION running from the neck to the feet, plus many small scattered components. That one region mixes t-shirt, trousers, shoes, skin, body contour, alpha antialiasing and generative variation together, so it separates nothing. A flat composite also cannot be inverted into overlapping layers: hair hides the cranium, the iris sits inside the eyes, blush is a blend mode, and pixels beneath the upper layers do not exist in the flat image.
pixelSourcePolicy.whyNoExactFigure: No exact pixel or component count is recorded here. The earlier figures were measured without pinning the difference metric, the alpha and colour thresholds or the 4- versus 8-connectivity, so they are not independently reproducible. The qualitative conclusion above is what this contract binds, and it is stable under every definition measured. If a numeric diagnostic is ever recorded, it must state metric, alpha threshold, colour threshold and connectivity in full.

hardMachine.format: exactly 1024x1536, RGBA, bit depth 8, colour type 6
hardMachine.protectedBody: exactly 0 differing RGBA bytes outside the approved head edit region after recomposition — H1's arms, hands, torso, top, shorts, legs and feet byte-identical
hardMachine.protectedTransition: exactly 0 differing bytes in the pre-registered neck/transition ring
hardMachine.background: alpha = 0 for every pixel outside the permitted figure/head envelope; no background, no shadow, no glow, no stray pixels, no unintended components
hardMachine.headRegion: no hair remains, no eyes, no iris, no brows, no nose, no mouth, no texture, symbols or accessories
hardMachine.provenance: pinned prompt, pinned inputs, pinned mask and mask semantics, documented recomposition, separate claim, full output hash and request id

ownerVisual: the head visually belongs to the same figure
skin tone and line style match the reference pair
gates.notCompared: The figure's global top and total height must NOT be compared directly with H1: removing the hair legitimately changes the topmost pixel. The body region is required to be byte-identical instead.
gates.noNewTolerances: No tolerance is set for ground contact, centre axis, body, hands, legs or feet in this call. After deterministic recomposition those regions must be byte-identical to H1 — the requirement is 0 differing pixels, not a tolerance.

sizeBudget.finding: SIZE_BUDGET_BYTES = 50 KB is defined in promote-r2-torso-asset.mjs and enforced only there and in avatar-r2-torso-asset-promotion.test.mjs, both on the TORSO asset (D-084 §5). The currently active runtime base body-neutral-medium-v2.webp is 67,174 B and already exceeds it. The constant is therefore not a base-layer gate and must not block the R3 underlay. File size is reported, not gated.

headMaskSuitability.verdict: USABLE AS THE EDIT REGION, BUT NOT ON ITS OWN — two documented gaps block the first image call.

gaps.finding: 445 H1 solid pixels above y433 fall OUTSIDE the mask, spread thinly over 283 rows from y20 to y433, at most 10 px in any row. All 445 differ from the target, and the target has 0 such pixels — so they are H1's own generated head fringe, not the pasted head. Protecting everything outside the mask byte-identically would let them survive as stray hair on a bald head.

The mask is strictly binary with no soft edge and no transition ring. Laterally it follows the figure exactly (mask span equals H1 span at y420-432), but its bottom is a hard horizontal cut at y433 — the neck line. The seam would be a straight horizontal line across the neck.

headMaskSuitability.consequence: No new mask has been created. Closing either gap needs a separate owner decision.
headMaskSuitability.resolution: CLOSED by D-133: GAP-1 by the bounded one-pixel dilation (G1, 445 px) and GAP-2 by transition candidate B (y425-445). See headEditRegions. The head-protect mask itself is unchanged and still byte-identical.
headMaskSuitability.prohibition: The fitting-base masks are fixtures from the fitting-base work. They are NOT automatically promoted to runtime masks. Any use as a reference or control when producing R3 assets must be documented separately.

headEditRegions.status: REGIONS APPROVED — FIXTURES TRACKED — NO IMAGE REQUEST AUTHORISED

rules.TRANSITION: H1solid ∩ { 425 <= y <= 445 } — candidate B, figure-clipped, not a rectangle

headEditRegions.whyBounded: The bounded dilation and the unbounded { H1solid and y <= 433 } union are measured identical on the pinned inputs (0 differing px). The bounded form is the approved one because it can never reach the neck or the body even if an input later changed.
headEditRegions.whyCandidateB: yTop 425 is the lowest row whose H1 width reaches round(73 x 1.50) = 110 px; yBot 445 is the midpoint of the measured stable neck column y436-454. The band straddles the neck line y433, so the seam lands inside the constant-width column instead of mid-taper. Candidates A (y429-440) and C (y416-450) were measured and rejected.

recomposition.transition: RGB ramped; alpha = H1's alpha byte-identical, so generated alpha never decides the silhouette
recomposition.ramp: denominator 20; num(y) = 445 - y; out = floor((num * generated + (20 - num) * h1 + 10) / 20) on 8-bit sRGB channels, round-half-up, integer only, no colour correction afterwards
recomposition.seamProperty: num(445) = 0, so the band's last row IS H1's own bytes, and y446 already lies in PROTECT: no generated residue survives at the y445/y446 boundary, by construction rather than by adjustment. The guarantee is per row against H1's own row and is NOT a claim that H1's rows 445 and 446 are byte-identical to each other.

gates.pre: generated and H1 must have an identical solid silhouette (alpha >= 128) across every pixel of rows 425-445
gates.postProtectedBytes: exactly 0 differing RGBA bytes against H1 inside PROTECT
gates.postNoLeak: no pixel outside EDIT originates from the generated image

recomposition.noRefit: No automatic warp, repair, region growth or after-the-fact adjustment of any region exists on this path.

fixtures.notRuntime: These are authoring fixtures. They are NOT runtime masks, carry no runtime authority and are not promoted by D-133.

headEditRegions.authorisation: D-133 and these fixtures authorise no image request and no claim.

armHandOcclusionContract.status: CONTRACT ONLY — NO REGION COMPUTED, NO MASK FIXTURE PRODUCED, NO IMAGE REQUEST AUTHORISED
armHandOcclusionContract.relationToD132: D-132's occlusionContract stated the invariant and made the pre-registration a precondition. D-134 fills in what that contract IS. It does not rewrite D-132, and it keeps D-132's own allowance that an approved garment MAY be deliberately authored to cover part of an arm or hand.

regions.R3_ARM_HAND_EXPOSED_BASE: The deterministically identified VISIBLE arm and hand surface of the approved R3 underlay, with the approved default clothing (tee, trousers, shoes) taken into account. It is a property of the approved base figure, not of any particular garment.

R3_INTENTIONAL_ARM_HAND_COVERAGE.mayBeNonEmpty: only after a separate owner decision for that one specific garment, naming the asset and the region
R3_INTENTIONAL_ARM_HAND_COVERAGE.d134ApprovesNone: D-134 approves NO non-empty intentional-coverage region for any asset.
R3_INTENTIONAL_ARM_HAND_COVERAGE.armorKnight: EMPTY under D-134. It becomes non-empty only if a later, separate decision says so.

regions.R3_ARM_HAND_PROTECT: R3_ARM_HAND_PROTECT(asset) := R3_ARM_HAND_EXPOSED_BASE \ R3_INTENTIONAL_ARM_HAND_COVERAGE(asset). With the default empty coverage this equals R3_ARM_HAND_EXPOSED_BASE, but the rule is written per asset so an approved exception narrows the protected region for that asset alone.

torsoFamily.precedent: the D-084/D-085 torso mask family; the same hard/edit/protect shape, not a new pattern

measurableRule.notAnUnconditionalBan: This is deliberately NOT a blanket prohibition on any garment pixel touching an arm or a hand. A future sleeve or glove that the owner has explicitly approved is expressed as a non-empty R3_INTENTIONAL_ARM_HAND_COVERAGE for that asset, which removes exactly that area from the protected region — and only for that asset. Without such a decision the coverage is empty and the three gates apply to the whole exposed surface.

armHandIdentification.yIntervalIsInsufficient: A Y-range alone is REJECTED as the identification rule. Torso, clothing and arms occupy many of the same rows, so rows cannot separate them. Any builder that isolates arms by row bounds alone is non-conforming.
mustUse: the approved separate alpha layers for tee, trousers and shoes
a fixed, pre-registered SPATIAL rule that isolates the left and right outer arm/hand components from the torso
8-connected component analysis with deterministic left/right hand seeds, or equivalently unambiguous pre-registered run/corridor rules
mustNotUse: a difference against the target figure as segmentation
the D-128 fitting-base arm/hand mask as runtime authority
any threshold or corridor chosen after seeing a candidate result
armHandIdentification.noAfterTheFactTuning: Seeds, corridors, tie-break rules and input hashes are fixed BEFORE the first real derivation runs. Choosing them once an output is on screen is the failure mode this clause exists to prevent.

feather.rule: edit = dilate(hard, at most 4 Master px), clipped to the figure's permitted area — the D-084/D-085 torso precedent, unchanged.
feather.neverIntoProtect: Feather may never enter R3_ARM_HAND_PROTECT(asset). Where a blend would land on exposed skin there is no blend at all, exactly as the collar zone is treated in build-r2-torso-occlusion-mask.mjs.
feather.exceptionIsPerAsset: A later intentional-coverage region can change this for that one asset only, and only by a separate owner decision.
feather.noRepair: No warp, no mask growth, no automatic repair, and no after-the-fact adjustment of any region.

authorisation.derivationMayRunWithoutANewImageAuthoris: Once the required approved R3 assets exist AND the deterministic builder is pre-registered with all seeds, corridors, tie-break rules and input hashes, the reproduction run itself may be performed without a further image authorisation. It is a deterministic derivation from approved raster inputs, not a generative call.
authorisation.notAcceptance: That is NOT automatic acceptance and NOT promotion.
stillRequired: the result may not be used for armour generation or runtime integration before it is approved
armor-knight's image call still needs separate authorisation and its own one-shot claim

implementationPrerequisites.note: NOTHING BELOW EXISTS YET. These are the preconditions D-134 registers, not artefacts it produces or verifies. No pixel region has been computed and no mask fixture has been written.
implementationPrerequisites.plannedBuilder: a deterministic tool, not yet written, whose seeds, corridors, tie-break rules and full input hashes must be pre-registered in its own spec before the first derivation run
implementationPrerequisites.productionOrder: these land at production step 11 (runtime masks and occlusion), after the garments at steps 8-10 exist

prohibitions.noRegionOrMask: D-134 creates no mask, no pixel region and no image asset.
prohibitions.noNonEmptyCoverageApproved: D-134 approves no non-empty intentional-coverage region for any asset, armor-knight included.

closedOwnerDecisions.was: whether blush is part of the first slice
closedOwnerDecisions.resolution: Fixed: blush is NOT part of the first slice, which is an isolated structural proof of geometry, alpha, layering, eyes, hair and the default clothing — deliberately incomplete, never completeR3Layers, never resolver-selectable, and never usable for canary, deploy or promotion. Blush remains MANDATORY at z=2 in the finished stack (D-135 unchanged) and is produced only after the first-slice gate, with its own automatic check and its own owner review before the stack may be called complete. The expected cheek-zone difference is qualitative diagnostic only, with no invented mask, ignored pixel count or new tolerance. Asset 8 keeps generated-or-constructed / 0-1 and the budget stays 15-16. See blushContract.

closedOwnerDecisions.was: the hairstyle contract: VALID_HAIRSTYLES and C2_HAIRSTYLES share only short, curly and long; afro is in the R2 manifest and in C2_HAIRSTYLES but not in VALID_HAIRSTYLES
closedOwnerDecisions.resolution: Fixed by an exact mapping table: absent, null, 'default' and 'tousled' resolve to northstar; 'short' and 'afro' to their own assets; the seven other valid stored values (braid, curly, long, sidecut, buzzcut, ponytail, buzz) return null, as does any invalid value INCLUDING the literal 'northstar', which is an asset key the live trigger rejects. A null means the whole stack falls back R3 -> R2 -> C2 rather than showing the wrong hair — a deliberate departure from R2, which always falls back to northstar. Shape only; the hair colour token is untouched. No stored-domain, Supabase, UI or R2 change, and no new asset or image call. See hairstyleContract.

closedOwnerDecisions.was: whether the iris is a colour token or its own generated asset
closedOwnerDecisions.resolution: Fixed: one independently generated achromatic luminance map multiplied by one independently pinned R3 token, R3_IRIS_DEFAULT = #A34A0F, with fixed-eyes on top in D-135's order. Asset 7 becomes method generated-luminance-map-plus-token with exactly 1 planned call, so the derived budget moves to 15-16. R2's untinted fail-soft is NOT carried over: missing tint support makes the R3 stack incomplete and the resolver must return null, falling back atomically R3 -> R2 -> C2. No EYE_COLOR system, identity field or persistence is introduced. See irisContract.

closedOwnerDecisions.was: the final z-index values for the three new clothing slots tee, trousers and shoes — the provisional 6, 7 and 8 are examples only and are not approved
closedOwnerDecisions.resolution: Fixed: tee 10, trousers 11, shoes 12, torso 20, with the whole R3 map pinned in zModel. The provisional 6, 7 and 8 are replaced because 6 and 8 are taken inside R3's own map by the eyes cosmetic and the face cosmetic.

closedOwnerDecisions.was: how the R3 clothing layers coexist with the current R2/C2 cosmetic stack, given that the provisional 6 and 8 collide numerically with the live R2_COSMETIC_Z (eyes cosmetic 6, face cosmetic 8) and that the provisional torso 20 is the C2 value rather than the live R2 torso-garment z of 1 — none of these numbers may be implemented before that decision
closedOwnerDecisions.resolution: Fixed: R3 gets its own independently pinned R3_STACK_Z and R3_COSMETIC_Z, never imported or aliased from R2/C2, and stack selection is atomic — completeR3Layers ?? completeR2Layers ?? composeC2Layers(...), complete-or-null, with no mixing of geometry-bound R2 and R3 layers. A cross-stack numeric overlap is explicitly permitted, because the three stacks never share a DOM.

closedOwnerDecisions.was: the R3 occlusion/protect contract that keeps exposed arms and hands clear of a torso or equipment layer, which must be pre-registered and approved before armor-knight is produced
closedOwnerDecisions.resolution: Closed as a CONTRACT. The protected region is R3_ARM_HAND_PROTECT(asset) := R3_ARM_HAND_EXPOSED_BASE \ R3_INTENTIONAL_ARM_HAND_COVERAGE(asset), whose coverage defaults to the empty set and may only become non-empty by a separate per-garment owner decision — so the rule is not an unconditional ban on future approved sleeves or gloves. Three zero-gates apply (finished garment pixels, hard-mask pixels, feather/edit-only pixels). A Y-interval alone is expressly rejected as the arm/hand identification rule. No region, mask or fixture is produced by D-134, and armor-knight is not released. See armHandOcclusionContract.

closedOwnerDecisions.was: how to close GAP-1 (445 stray H1 head-fringe pixels outside the mask)
closedOwnerDecisions.resolution: G1 := ( dilate8(E0,1) ∩ H1solid ∩ { y <= 433 } ) \ E0 — 445 px, of which 444 are head/edge fringe and exactly one, at (475,433), is neck contour; CORE_BASE := E0 ∪ G1 — 124,544 px, one 8-connected component.

closedOwnerDecisions.was: how to close GAP-2 (no transition ring; hard horizontal seam at the neck line y433)
closedOwnerDecisions.resolution: TRANSITION := H1solid ∩ { 425 <= y <= 445 } — candidate B, 1,702 px over 21 rows, straddling the neck line y433 and ending inside the stable neck column y436-454.
